newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-D.Jones sees profit drop not as bad.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-D.Jones sees profit drop not as bad.

text.p: David Jones Ltd managing director Chris Tideman said on Tuesday the weak outlook for the company's first half net profit had improved after good trading results in the month of January.

Asked if the company still expected to report half year net earnings 50 percent below that for the previous year, Tideman said: "It will not be as bad as that (50 percent), that's all I can really say."

David Jones earlier said that its sales for the 26 weeks ended January 25 fell one percent to A$782.6 million, but that January sales were significantly above the same month in 1996, improving the year to date figures from a negative 2.9 percent variance as at the end of December.

In early January, David Jones lowered its first half profit forecast to lower revenues and higher depreciation charges and pointed to a lacklustre retail trading environment, despite good Christmas week trading.
David Jones reported a net profit of A$44.64 million for the six months to January 27, 1996 on sales of A$790.31 million.
"I think a 40 percent drop (in first half net profit) is a more realistic figure now," a Sydney-based analyst said.
The analyst said the company's clearance sales were a significant factor in January and the company needed to sustain its January sales growth to significant improve its full year profit outlook.
At 1.20 p.m. (0220 GMT), David Jones shares were one cents weaker at A$1.47.
